items.title: Karnataka records 4,212 influenza cases; Health Dept says H1N1 rise is seasonal
items.summary: Karnataka has recorded 4,212 laboratory-confirmed influenza cases across 32 districts so far this year, with the Health Department attributing the current rise in H1N1 cases to the state’s usual seasonal pattern and urging people not to panic. According to surveillance data from the Integrated Health Information Platform (IHIP), 4,212 influenza cases had been confirmed in the state as of August 22, 2026. H1N1 is a strain of the influenza A virus that can cause seasonal flu. Common symptoms include fever, cough, sore throat, body ache and fatigue. Bengaluru accounts for the majority of the cases. The Greater Bengaluru Authority (MSU) area has reported 2,070 cases so far this year, compared to 2,587 in 2025 and 1,189 in 2024. Bengaluru Urban has recorded 1,011 cases, broadly comparable to 961 cases in 2025 and 991 in 2024. The Health Department said influenza generally records two seasonal peaks in Karnataka — between January and March and again between July and September. The current increase in cases therefore falls within the state's usual seasonal pattern.
